findings.title: Suite 3 emergency commands omit source and stated word-count validation
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The emergency creation path accepts input outside PCK-1 before its expensive KDF. This must be corrected before claiming these shipped emergency tools enforce the specification input contract. Coordinator makes the final release decision.

reproduction.stdin:
abandon abandon ability
public audit password
public audit password
reproduction.setup: Load the unchanged module; replace openssl_argon2id only with a recording boundary that raises ArgonBoundary before any KDF. Run python-contracts-probe.py in normal mode.
reproduction.secondCase: suite3.main(["decrypt", "13"]) with the published zero-12 container and the same synthetic password.

findings.expected: Reject the three-word source and the unsupported stated length before reaching Argon2.
findings.observed: Normal mode decodes abandon abandon ability to four zero bytes and reaches the Argon2 boundary once. Stated length 13 also reaches the boundary once. No Argon2 call or final encrypted output was executed.
findings.impact: Unsupported source data enters the expensive encryption path; its four-byte source length cannot be represented by the specified recovery lengths. Unsupported stated lengths also waste a full recovery. This is not a demonstrated loss of an existing valid wallet.
findings.recommendedFix: Validate source token counts before BIP39 bit decoding, and validate stated recovery counts against {0,12,15,18,21,24} before permutation work. Keep checksum and count rejection independent.
findings.requiredVerification: Boundary tests for all supported lengths and 3, 11, 13, 25 words, including the public three-word counterexample; invalid stated counts must make zero KDF calls. Verify existing published valid sources retain their bytes.

findings.title: Both emergency suites pass out-of-range PIM and MEM to the KDF boundary
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The shipped emergency entrypoints do not enforce WF-2 and can attempt settings compatible implementations refuse. Final release acceptance belongs to the coordinator.

reproduction.inputs: Published zero-12 / same-length-nonzero-12 phrases or containers and a synthetic public password. Repeat each with PIM 0, MEM 22.
reproduction.setup: Recording Argon boundary raises before any cryptography operation; see python-contracts-probe.py.

findings.expected: All eight upper-bound-invalid cases are refused locally with zero KDF calls.
findings.observed: Each of eight cases reaches the Argon boundary exactly once carrying PIM 1024 or MEM 22. The pass formula maps PIM 1024 to 12300 passes, without a suite-range check.
findings.impact: PIM 1024 can enter a nonconforming creation/recovery computation; MEM 22 is not rejected by the script before invoking its KDF adapter. No allocation or successful derivation at MEM 22 is claimed: a dependency may reject that value later. Negative values can already fail in unsigned encoding, so this finding does not claim every invalid integer is accepted.
findings.recommendedFix: Use a shared explicit PIM/MEM validator before source permutation and before constructing a KDF. State supported memory levels and enforce a resource limit without reducing protocol parameters.
findings.requiredVerification: Check omitted/default 0, valid endpoints 1023/21, invalid -1/1024 and -1/22 using a recording KDF boundary; invalid values must make zero calls. Do not execute large valid endpoints merely to test validation.

findings.title: A matching stated length hides every other matching source length
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The selected reading remains the specified one. The defect omits an ambiguity diagnostic; it is not evidence that the chosen wallet has been authenticated.
findings.expected: Select the 12-word reading and separately name the 21-word match.
findings.observed: matching_short_lengths returns [12,21]; stated_recovery returns only the 12-word tuple. The CLI emits only those returned tuples and has no separate ambiguity diagnostic. No KDF is needed to reproduce this post-permutation decision.
findings.impact: The owner is not told that another layout passes the source verifier. No-stated-length recovery still returns all short matches plus the unverified 24-word reading, so REC-2 is not universally broken.
findings.recommendedFix: Keep the chosen reading separate from metadata listing every detected matching length, and emit that metadata in the CLI.
findings.requiredVerification: Use the published ambiguous 12/21, 15/21 and 18/21 states with each matching and nonmatching stated length, plus 0 and 24. Assert selected readings and all additional reported lengths.

findings.title: Emergency suite 3 recovery never evaluates the mandatory 16-bit wallet check
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The CLI conservatively labels 24-word readings not verified and asks for a known-address comparison. Missing advisory status is a current conformance omission, not a false claim that a wallet identity is verified. Coordinator should settle whether emergency scope is intentionally narrower and document it explicitly.
findings.expected: The recovered phrase stays not verified, with an additional passing 16-bit wallet-check status under empty Q.
findings.observed: The post-permutation recovery returns only a (24,False,phrase) tuple; decrypt and main neither compute a BIP39 seed/wallet digest nor report any 16-bit status. The public profile checker independently reproduces the passing digest. This is static entrypoint tracing plus a post-permutation public-case probe, not a newly executed full-cost recovery.
findings.impact: The emergency path omits information required by REC-3 for owners who deliberately used the profile. It does not silently certify another wallet; profile support is not claimed to provide authentication.
findings.recommendedFix: Evaluate and report the profile check on every 24-word reading with Unicode 18 normalization and an entered or empty BIP39 passphrase, while preserving the not-verified identity label. If emergency tools intentionally remain partial, explicitly resolve/document their conformance exception instead of claiming complete suite recovery.
findings.requiredVerification: Use passing and failing profile vectors with empty Q and TREZOR. Check the 24-word candidate in ambiguous-length recovery too; no short reading should be marked as wallet identity verified.

findings.title: Release-archive claims include emergency scripts absent from the existing v0.7.0 tagged source tree
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Low documentary mismatch, with no mandatory runtime integrity failure demonstrated. Publishing the audited additions under the unchanged old tag would remain an unresolved provenance/acceptance problem until the owner selects the intended release source.

reproduction.observed: The existing tag peels to 1b90529bd5e40c2d3ef7197d3c3ca88e175a4d5d, not audited HEAD 13215935bcdd320539a93e678cec374ba556528f. Both script paths and their packaged prerequisites are absent; the profile JSON and requirement-checker additions are also absent.
reproduction.execution: Read-only Git commands freshly executed in this review.

findings.expected: Documentation qualifies which published/tagged archives contain these files and identifies unreleased additions accurately. A release advertised as containing the new emergency path must actually contain that path and its prerequisites.
findings.observed: Current wording unconditionally promises availability from every release archive while the existing version-named source tree lacks the files. Local tag/tree evidence establishes the content mismatch; no custom uploaded archive was inspected.
findings.impact: A reader following long-term recovery guidance can save the version-named source archive expecting an independent emergency implementation and discover later that it is absent. HEAD has the implementation; no lost-funds scenario or bad recovery result is demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Qualify archive claims to actual applicable versions and label untagged additions as pending. For publication, explicitly choose and document a version/tag that identifies the reviewed source. Do not silently move or recreate the existing signed tag; any version/tag/release mutation is the owner-authorized coordinator phase.
requiredVerification: Compare intended release tag peeled commit/tree against the audited source fingerprint.
Check the actual final source/recovery archive includes both scripts, hashed requirements, BIP39 list and license, profile JSON/checker and requirement-ID/checker material promised for that version.
Confirm the public release URL/status and attached PDF verification record refer to that source; keep pending publication separate from historical evidence.
Regenerate/review PDF wording only in a separately authorized remediation phase if README wording changes.

informationalNotes: The fresh dependency audit reported pdfjs-dist 5.6.205 (GHSA-hq66-cqwq-w95j; upstream high) and markdown-it 15.0.2 (GHSA-gfr2-rv44-r23c high; GHSA-vfgh-jcmw-g37q low). The PDF.js advisory needs browser viewer scripting; this build uses Node getDocument/render of newly generated PDFs, not that viewer. The Markdown advisories require adversarial Markdown; the build consumes trusted checked-in documents and runs inside a network-disabled, resource-bounded container. No application compromise was established. Update the pinned PDF dependencies in a separate verified change; do not present the nonzero scanner result as a clean scan. Primary sources: https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/security/advisories/GHSA-hq66-cqwq-w95j and https://github.com/markdown-it/markdown-it/security/advisories/GHSA-gfr2-rv44-r23c and https://github.com/markdown-it/markdown-it/security/advisories/GHSA-vfgh-jcmw-g37q.

Python optimization (-O or PYTHONOPTIMIZE) removes assertions, including the inverse creation call and fixture comparisons. This is not the documented invocation and was not promoted to a normal-runtime High finding. Explicitly reject that mode or replace mandatory boundary/integrity assertions if supporting it; tampered-fixture successes in that mode remain local evidence.

Static creation conformance is narrower than the normative six-step procedure: emergency encrypt inverts raw Y before word encoding, does not decode the final words for that check, and does not explicitly refuse Y=X. No real fixed-point, encoder defect or cryptographic fault was produced; a fabricated failure of trusted code was not treated as an exploit. Align these steps or explicitly document the narrower emergency scope when changing creation.

The profile checker uses the host Unicode database, while its present fixtures use ASCII passphrases. Its current vector checks remain valid; a newly assigned non-ASCII passphrase needs the prescribed Unicode18 normalization. Do not reuse the helper as a general wallet-check implementation without that change.

The exact deniability experiment has only its stated inputs. Arbitrary auxiliary advice correlated with the undisclosed password is not proved harmless: the one-bit advice example concerns an extension outside that game, not a refutation of the current theorem. Existing model limitations and open cases remain necessary.

Git fetch failed because a local refs/codex/turn-diffs checkpoint references a bad object. No ref or configuration was repaired. Separate public metadata confirms the remote main/tag state. This environmental problem is not a cryptographic finding.

The two audit-harness weaknesses found during review (substring-only recovery comparison and newest-directory contact-sheet selection) were corrected and independently compensated using exact saved stdout and the matching per-attempt successful verification/PDF hashes. No successful expensive KDF run was repeated just for that oracle change.

A late static allegation that unknown phrase tokens are echoed by list.index errors was not reproduced on the audited Python 3.14.4: four actual encrypt/decrypt refusals returned the neutral message list.index(x): x not in list, without the synthetic token in STDERR. The allegation was not added as a current finding. Interpreter-version behavior outside that executed scope remains untested.

limitations: No formal proof verification, independent human cryptographer certification, concrete PRP/SPRP proof or proof of Argon2 physical memory/time cost.

Historical complete Argon2 replays bind the current fixture bytes to their historical verifier/environment. New execution covers four default-cost emergency CLI operations, not every current full-cost vector/negative case or extreme work factor.

The passwords command does not execute the separate JavaScript boundary, five settings, six phrase and eight length-detection rows of the suite 3 conformance file. Selected direct boundary/model checks and static review are recorded; not every one of those rows was freshly exercised through the current emergency CLI.
A retained Core test log used a project-copy method in the interrupted attempt. It was not rerun or treated as new in-place implementation verification.
All pages were visually screened at contact-sheet size; only recorded critical samples were inspected at full size. Automated syntax/text/raster checks do not prove mathematical meaning.
Version-matched dependency advisories are recorded with reachability limits. No hostile PDF or denial-of-service exploit was executed.
Git fetch failed on an invalid local Codex checkpoint reference; it was not repaired. Public GitHub tag/main/release metadata was read separately.
Static workflow review and local controlled build do not prove a successful remote CI/release run. No remote CI job was dispatched.
No production fix, vector change, tracked PDF replacement, commit, push, tag, release or publication was performed. Research/novelty recommendations are outside this formal audit record.

Checked there with a stubbed Argon2id boundary: 3- and 13-word sources, stated length 13, a 12-word suite 3 container, PIM -1/1024 and memory level 22 are refused with zero KDF calls in both suites; PIM 1023 with memory level 21 passes validation; the published ambiguous 12/21 state with stated length 12 names the 21-word match; a full-cost decrypt of vectors/suite3/zero-12.json recovers its source; all 17 suite 3 vectors reproduce with recorded keys.
